title: Hard edge, soft spine
style: documentary photograph, working forge, firelight, deep shadow, muted colour, fine grain, no text, no watermark, no modern tools
negative: text, letters, words, watermark, logo, cartoon, cgi, painting, illustration, modern workshop, safety equipment

lines.vo: A medieval sword was never cast. It was forged from a bar of iron.
lines.image: a rough iron billet on an anvil

lines.vo: The smith worked it near twelve hundred degrees. Orange, not yellow.
lines.image: glowing steel drawn from a charcoal fire

lines.vo: Iron with too little carbon bends. Iron with too much shatters on the first parry.
lines.image: a broken blade section, dark metal

lines.vo: So the blade is built in layers. Hard steel at the edge, soft iron in the spine.
lines.image: an etched blade showing a layered pattern

lines.vo: Hammer and fold, again and again. Each fold doubles the layers.
lines.image: a hammer striking bright steel, sparks

lines.vo: Then the finished blade is heated once more and plunged into oil.
lines.image: a quench tank, dark oil, smoke

lines.vo: The thin edge cools in under a second and locks hard. The spine stays soft.
lines.image: steam rising off dark oil in a low room

lines.vo: A sword that is hard the whole way through is a sword that snaps.
lines.image: a snapped blade lying on stone

lines.vo: Two hundred hours of work, and the design is entirely in how fast it cooled.
lines.image: a finished blade on a workbench, low light
lines.title: TWO HUNDRED HOURS
lines.footer: and all of it is in the cooling
